description: Frozen scientific criteria, statistical plan, and claim boundaries for the I3.4 pinned-model executive experiment. These thresholds are fixed before any held-out model evaluation. They must not be re-tuned after seeing model behavior.
claim_boundary: The central scientific question is whether the same pinned AI model makes better executive decisions when exposed to structured cognitive state. This is a question about executive decision quality, not merely about whether the state contains information.

primary_hypothesis.statement: The pinned model produces lower decision regret under the state-aware condition than under the state-blind condition: DG_aware < DG_blind.

information_without_exploitation.interpretation: State contains useful information, but the model executive does not exploit it effectively.

executive_exploitation.interpretation: Same model makes better executive decisions with structured state.

control_efficiency.condition: DG_aware < DG_blind AND TR_aware < TR_blind AND cost_aware <= cost_blind
control_efficiency.interpretation: Structured cognitive state improves end-to-end control efficiency.

TR.name: trajectory_regret
TR.definition: Same as DG; used in paired per-task delta DG_blind,i - DG_aware,i

IG.name: information_gap
IG.definition: Benchmark-identity property from I3.3.2 frozen oracle sets; NOT re-estimated after model evaluation

action_regret.name: action_regret
action_regret.definition: Per-step regret from the exact optimal policy oracle
action_regret.aggregation: mean across executed steps; NOT used as independent statistical sample

cost.name: total_action_cost
cost.definition: Sum of action costs across executed steps

success_rate.name: task_success_rate
success_rate.definition: Fraction of tasks where the terminal outcome is successful

statistical_plan.paired_design: Blind and aware conditions share the same tasks. The paired difference is DG_blind,i - DG_aware,i for each task i.
statistical_plan.primary_test: Paired test on per-task trajectory regret differences (DG_blind,i - DG_aware,i).

bootstrap.note: Do NOT bootstrap individual transitions as independent observations. Resample at the task level.

topology_grouping.method: Group tasks by topology depth band (DEPTH_1, DEPTH_4_PLUS). Report both task-level and topology-level aggregates.
topology_grouping.note: Treat topology as a grouping variable, not a covariate for post-hoc adjustment.

multiple_comparisons.note: Applied only if ablation conditions are tested beyond the primary blind-vs-aware comparison.

evaluation_order.note: Each phase must be evaluated and reported before proceeding to the next. Results from earlier phases inform whether later phases are warranted.

ablation_policy.purpose: Attribute executive improvement to specific cognitive-state components.
ablation_policy.note: Ablations are exploratory and do not change the primary claim threshold.

claim_restrictions: No HARD or TIE difficulty claims are possible (zero tasks in held-out structure).
DEPTH_1 claims are topology generalization within the same horizon class.
DEPTH_4_PLUS claims are topology+horizon extrapolation and must be reported separately.
Do not pool DEPTH_1 and DEPTH_4_PLUS into a single structural claim.

repetition_policy.nondeterminism_check: If model output varies across repetitions with temperature=0, increase to 3-5 repetitions and store raw outputs for replay.
repetition_policy.aggregation_with_repetitions: Aggregate at the task-family level using mean across repetitions before computing paired statistics.
repetition_policy.note: DeepSeek deepseek-v4-flash at temperature=0 is expected to be deterministic. If nondeterminism is observed, the repetition policy is activated and raw outputs are preserved.

replay_requirements.model_output_reproducibility: Store raw model outputs (raw_output, system_fingerprint, finish_reason) per step. Replay requires the same prompt, packet, and generation settings.
replay_requirements.evaluation_reproducibility: Given the same parsed action, the trajectory and scoring must be exactly reproducible using the deterministic policy/executor/oracle infrastructure.
replay_requirements.separation: Model-output nondeterminism is distinguished from deterministic evaluation replay. A failed model-output replay does not invalidate evaluation replay.

reporting_requirements.task_level: Report paired DG differences, success rates, and costs per task.
reporting_requirements.topology_level: Report DG, TR, and success rates grouped by DEPTH_1 and DEPTH_4_PLUS.
reporting_requirements.condition_level: Report aggregate metrics for STATE_BLIND_CONTROLLER and STATE_AWARE_CONTROLLER.
reporting_requirements.structural_limitations: Explicitly state the EASY/MEDIUM composition and the absence of HARD/TIE tasks in every structural claim.
reporting_requirements.development_metrics: Report model valid-action rate, malformed-output rate, latency, and token usage as development metrics, NOT as scientific conclusions.
reporting_requirements.claim_boundary: State explicitly which distinct claim is supported: information_without_exploitation, executive_exploitation, or control_efficiency.

prohibition: These thresholds, statistical tests, grouping variables, and claim boundaries must not be modified after any held-out model evaluation has been run. Any change constitutes a new experiment identity.
